subject: Coffee & Tea
title: Espresso Roast vs. Filter Roast
description: A micro-lesson that makes Espresso Roast vs. Filter Roast usable.

hook.text: Espresso and filter coffee extract differently—so the same bean is often roasted to different levels for each method.

buildup.text: Espresso pushes pressurized water through fine grounds in 25–30 seconds. It extracts intensely and amplifies acidity.

discovery.text: Espresso roasts are typically pushed slightly darker to reduce sharp acidity and increase solubility for the short extraction.

twist.text: Filter roasts can stay lighter because longer brew times (3–5 minutes) extract gently—acidity is balanced naturally.

climax.text: Omni-roast tries to work for both methods. It's a compromise that many roasters attempt but few master perfectly.

punchline.text: Espresso needs darker. Filter can stay light. Brew method dictates roast.

quiz.question: Why are espresso roasts typically darker than filter roasts?
options: Short, pressurized extraction amplifies acidity—darker roast compensates
